newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes firm in light pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes firm in light pre-holiday trade.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes held firm in light pre-holiday trade Monday afternoon, while sour and sweet grade differentials were steady to weaker.

A cold wave across Europe has lifted outright prices. Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for February was trading around $25.35-45 a barrel, up five cents from this morning and 20 cents from late Friday's cash market.
The Feb/Mar WTI spread climbed three cents from this morning to 71 cents.
The NYMEX closes early at 1300 EST December 31 and will reopen for a regular session on January 2.
Grade activity picked up slightly from this morning, although many traders remain on vacation until after New Year's.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James changed hands at 39 cents premium to WTI/Cushing, even with Friday's activity but two cents stronger than a deal done this morning.
Midland/WTI was traded at WTI/Cushing minus one cent, steady with Friday's notional range.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded at WTI/Cushing minus $1.53 a barrel, three cents under a deal done this morning and one transacted last Friday.
Separately, the United Nations gave the green light to another Iraqi oil contract under the oil-for-food program, raising the total number of contracts approved to 21.
